Browser DevTools mastery (used in every phase) · 8/8

Read the longest phase first

  1. 1Long Waiting (TTFB): look at the server
  2. 2Long Content Download: file size or network
  3. 3Long Queueing: too many requests compete

Open the Network panel, click one request, and open the Timing tab.

It splits the request into phases.

The phases run in this order: Queueing, Stalled,

DNS Lookup, Initial connection, Request sent, Waiting, and Content Download.

Queueing and Stalled are waits.

The request waits for higher-priority requests,

a free connection, or disk cache space.

DNS Lookup finds the server IP address.

Initial connection covers the TCP handshakes and the SSL negotiation.

Waiting, or TTFB, is one round trip plus server time.

In this example, a slow server makes Waiting the longest bar.

Now set Throttling to Slow 4G.

Waiting and Content Download grow,

because each round trip and each byte is slower.

Disable cache makes a first visit.

Turn it off and reload:

a repeat visit loads files from the browser cache instead.

Read the longest phase first.

Long Waiting points at the server,

long Content Download at size or network, long Queueing at competition.
